plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control DE on TPM with limma
plan.analytical_narrative: The delivered data is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample gene-level TPM table from Salmon (6 psoriasis lesional vs 6 control skin samples, unpaired, single batch) plus a 12x2 metadata table; no raw counts and no quantification directories were delivered. Count-based models (DESeq2, edgeR, voom) are therefore not applicable: TPM abundances violate the integer-count negative-binomial variance assumption they require (rule R-0004@a06d). The procedure for TPM/FPKM input is limma with trend=TRUE on log2-transformed values, which is what this plan runs. Flow: (1) sample-structure QC on log2(TPM+1) to verify the TPM table's sample columns match metadata rows 1:1 and that the condition contrast is not compromised by outliers or sample swaps; (2) an abundance floor filter (>=1 TPM in at least the smallest group size, 6 samples) to cut the multiple-testing burden and untrustworthy fold changes, log2(TPM+1) as the only transform, then a limma linear model with control as the explicit reference level and a named lesional-vs-control contrast, moderated with eBayes(robust=TRUE, trend=TRUE); (3) DE selection by BH-adjusted p < 0.05, plus an effect-size-anchored list from treat(lfc=1) tested inside the model, and a report with the full ranked table, plots, and reproducibility record. No LFC shrinkage step is included: the procedure leaves shrink_lfc uncovered for TPM/log-value input, so moderated log2FC are reported as estimated. A data-limitation caveat carries through the whole plan: inference on TPM-only input is weaker than on raw counts and TPM is a within-sample relative abundance (compositional effects can shift apparent abundance), so results should be re-validated on raw counts if they are later provided.
